sentences.text:
Applicant :- Guddu Yadav
Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. And 3 Others
Counsel for Applicant :- Virendra Kumar Yadav,Amarnath Tripathi,Shipra Kureel,Sudhir Kum

Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.
1.
Sri Suresh Bahadur Singh, learned AGA-I for the State apprised the Court that on 7.7.2022 notice has been served to the informant of the case.
2. Despite service of notice, none appeared on behalf of the informant.

3. Heard Sri Sudhir Kumar Agarwal, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Suresh Bahadur Singh, learned AGA-I for the State-respondent.
4.

The instant application has been filed seeking release of the applicant on bail in Case Crime No.
127 of 2021, under Sections 363, 366, 376 IPC and 3/4 POCSO Act, Police Station- Ali Nagar,
District- Chandauli, during pendency of the trial in the court below.
5. This is the second bail application filed on behalf of the applicant.

The first bail application of the applicant has been dismissed on 16.5.2022 for non prosecution and according to the FIR, applicant and other accused persons abducted the daughter of the informant from her house in her absence.

sentences.text: 1 6. Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that although, technically this is the second bail application but first bail application of the applicant was not dismissed on merit and it was dismissed for non prosecution.

He further submitted that although, victim is minor and she in her statement recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. made allegation of rape against the applicant but when she appeared before the trial court then she did not make any accusation against the applicant and her statement recorded by the trial court has been annexed as Annexure No. SA-2 to the supplementary affidavit and applicant is not having any criminal history and is in jail since 12.5.2022 i.e. for last about 2 years, therefore, he may be released on bail.
7.

Per contra, learned AGA although, opposed the prayer for bail but could not dispute the fact that applicant is in jail in the present matter for last about more than two years and victim of the case appeared before the trial court and has turned hostile.
8. I have heard both the parties and perused the record of the case.
9. Technically this is the second bail application but first bail application of the applicant was dismissed for non prosecution.

Although, victim appears to be a minor girl and she in her statement recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. made allegation of rape against the applicant but when she appeared before the trial court as P.W. 2 then she did not support her earlier version and she has declared hostile and applicant is in jail in the present matter since May, 2021 i.e. for last about more than two years.
10. Therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case discussed above, in my view applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
11. Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant bail application is allowed.

12. Let the applicant- Guddu Yadav be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the dates fixed, unless his personal presence is exempted.
(ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly, make inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal and anti-social activity.
13.
In case of breach of any of the above condition, the prosecution will be at liberty to move an application before this Court for cancellation of the bail of the applicant.
